The Government reserves the right to invite to Phase II only those Go-rated offerors whose submissions demonstrate the highest technical merit and lowest operational transition risk. A submission that does not meet all Go criteria will receive a No-Go rating and will not advance. 3.3 Phase II Preview — Oral Presentation, Demonstration, and Targeted Validation The Government may invite selected vendors receiving a Phase I Go rating to participate in Phase II oral presentations, live demonstrations, technical challenges, written question- and-answer exchanges, or a comb

ombination of these methods. Phase II instructions and evaluation criteria will be provided only to selected vendors. To validate solution maturity, feasibility, and alignment with Government objectives, the Government may request one or more of the following: 1. Oral presentation or live demonstration of relevant commercial capabilities; 2. Clariﬁcation or reﬁnement of the Technical Solution Brief, Draft SOO Crosswalk, or draft performance-based work statement; 3. A proposed performance-measurement and surveillance approach addressing key operational, cybersecurity, modernization, and delivery outcomes; 4. A high-level resource and staffing approach; 5. A preliminary ROM or other commercial-pricing information; and 6. Additional information needed to assess technical viability, commercial feasibility, technology readiness, cost-effectiveness, and the appropriate potential acquisition pathway. Phase II may assess the following: 1. Technical viability and maturity: Whether the solution is commercially mature, technically feasible, and capable of meeting the Government’s objectives. 2. Operations and modernization approach: Whether the proposed approach credibly sustains legacy operations, cybersecurity, and partner interoperability while modernizing DxP capabilities. 3

Phase III Preview — Detailed Commercial Proposal The Government may invite selected Phase II vendors to submit a detailed commercial proposal. Detailed Phase III instructions, evaluation criteria, and any requested pricing information will be provided only to vendors selected to proceed. Based on the Government’s assessment of the selected solution and the anticipated acquisition pathway, Phase III may require: 1. A reﬁned technical solution and performance-based work statement; 2. A detailed performance-surveillance approach addressing key operational, cybersecurity, modernization, and delivery outcomes; 3. A detailed resource and staffing plan; 4. A transition-in plan and integrated delivery schedule; 5. Detailed pricing, ROM reﬁnement, or cost information appropriate to the contemplated award instrument; 6. A reﬁned OCI mitigation plan; and 7. Other information necessary to establish ﬁnal award terms. The Government may use the Phase III submission to determine the appropriate acquisition approach and potential award terms.
